analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Semis rally debate; Telia acquisition; Technoprobe look through; TEF solid; UTDI inline; Stroer misses; Amadeus
key_insights: US semiconductors are bouncing. The SOX has rebounded nearly 20% from its lows but remains about 25% below its YTD highs. AMD gained 40% in four days. The desk sees hedge funds and long-only investors starting to chase the recovery, while similar buying has not yet emerged in Europe.

The Nasdaq 100 has reclaimed its 200-day moving average and pre-election levels as positioning improves and volatility eases. NDX was up about 225bps on the day with VIX at a 17 handle. The SOX is approaching its own 200-day moving average.
GS Prime data shows Systematic long/short funds posted their strongest two-day returns in almost three years.

Nvidia is the exception in semis, down 8% after hours on a WSJ report that the board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang, with alleged further affairs including with staff. Asia Pacific equities slipped 0.5% after a three-day rally, with TSMC and Hynix down and Samsung up.

Telia is acquiring the Telavox B2B customer base (24k mainly SME businesses, 325k end-users) across four Nordic countries. Closing is expected in 1Q27 and Telia will need to sell the Danish part. Per Telia it is SEK400mn accretive in 2028 pre-financing costs, implying roughly 3-3.5% consensus upgrades. The FY27 SEK10bn FCF target is unchanged. The desk sees a small negative for Telenor, since Telavox uses Telia and Telenor in Sweden and Telenor in Norway.

United Airlines is banning AI agents from making flight reservations on behalf of travellers, citing security risks and possible violation of federal rules. Similar headlines have appeared for bank transactions and other industries in recent weeks.
Amadeus is worth watching: press reports that Travelport stakeholders are discussing paths forward, including a combination with Sabre. The desk says this should be positive for Amadeus.

Microsoft pledged to fund data-centre power without government subsidies or passing costs to other electricity consumers (Noelle Walsh: 'pay our own way'). The pledge addresses post-midterm political risks and local opposition, and signals hyperscalers may absorb higher power costs.

Technoprobe Q3 revenue and EBITDA beat by 3% and 4%, but Q4/FY26 guidance was below Street. Q4 revenue guidance of EUR270mn implies FY26 revenue of EUR1.05-1.065bn versus EUR1.1bn consensus. The company told the desk the lower Q4 is a one-off from a 4-day ERP shutdown. The Cernusco plant was completed in Q4, ahead of its Q1 2027 schedule, and annual capacity is targeted at EUR2bn by end-2027, supported by EUR150-200mn of additional capex in H2 2027. Management gave no formal 2027 guidance. AI demand remains robust with growing HBM opportunities.

Telefonica Q3 beat on revenue (1.3%), EBITDAaL (1.7%) and FCF. FY guidance changes: revenue growth lowered to 1%-1.5% from 1.5%-2.5%, adjusted EBITDA raised to slightly above 2.5% from 1.5%-2.5%, adjusted OpCFaL raised to over 3.5% from over 3%, and FCF raised to about EUR3.1bn from about EUR3.0bn. Spain KPIs and momentum are solid. Germany is light, with EBITDA 2.2% below expectations, and TEF says it improves in 2027. Net debt is higher.

TEF FCF was EUR1.02bn versus EUR821mn consensus, including a EUR300mn tax benefit that some of the Street had included and some had not, so the size of the true beat is unclear. OFCF beat on lower capex due to phasing.

United Internet (UTDI) beat revenue by 1% and was in line on EBITDA, with guidance reiterated. The debate will be on restructuring costs at 1&1 and what was in consensus. IONOS was in line with a slight EBITDA beat on cost cutting, guidance reiterated, with strong adds but high marketing spend. 1&1 was in line on revenue, EBITDA was messy but a beat excluding restructuring costs, capex was a bit higher, and guidance was reiterated.

Freenet 3Q26 revenue and EBITDA were broadly in line and FCF beat on tax timing. FY26 guidance was reiterated. Higher tax payments as loss carry-forwards expire are increasingly likely to slip into 2027, so Freenet expects 2026 FCF at the midpoint to upper end of its EUR270-300mn range versus EUR282mn company-compiled consensus. Finalising MNO negotiations remains the bigger catalyst. A waipu.tv IPO is now ruled out following the minority buyout.

Stroer Q3 missed. Revenue of EUR513mn was 2% below GS estimates and consensus, with organic growth of 0.8% versus 3.8% expected, reflecting weakness across all segments. Operating EBITDA of about EUR148mn was broadly in line, with margin of 28.8% versus 28.4%/28.2% expected, and adjusted net income of about EUR35mn beat GS's EUR33mn. No Q4 outlook was given, and FY26 guidance was reiterated, which the desk expects to be under pressure.
Away from GS: SAP was upgraded to Overweight by JPM, and Auto Trader was raised to Buy from Hold by Berenberg.

Fractile, a UK AI inference chip startup, raised a $720mn Series C led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Lightspeed and Redpoint, with backing from Britain's Sovereign AI Fund. The government puts its valuation above GBP5bn while FT and Reuters report $7bn. First chips and systems are to ship in 2027.

South Korea will invest W440.2bn in humanoid robotics: W100bn for actuators, W271.4bn for batteries enabling 8-hour operation by 2031, and W68.8bn for on-sensor AI. Korea's FSC is expected to hold a symposium at the KRX on KOSDAQ measures: mandatory IR presentations, a market-cap based delisting system and tiering. Samsung is partnering with AMD on semiconductor testing, integrating Samsung memory and storage with AMD EPYC Embedded 9006 processors.

INWIT's call focused on contract disputes. Management welcomes action by AGCM (antitrust review of the Telecom Italia/Swisscom tower JV), CONSOB (says INWIT did not undergo a change of control in 2020) and AGCOM (seeking talks between Telecom Italia and INWIT). An AGCOM-facilitated meeting could take place as early as 26 November, a potential positive catalyst.

Auto Trader: dealers saw a 30% surge in pre-registered cars advertised in October, adding competition for used car retailers. Netflix reaches 67% of US internet households, up from 64% a year earlier, and HBO Max overtook Paramount+.

Callahan's read: the move is an output of cleaner positioning, volatility resetting lower and election narratives being digested. There is little consensus in the market, with debate on where the AI/semi cycle stands and whether this is a bear-market bounce or a forming bull market. Software dispersion has picked up and Internet has become squeezy and difficult to trade.

market_movers.rationale: Down 8% after hours on a WSJ report that the board is preparing to remove Jensen Huang, with alleged further affairs including with staff.
Up 40% in four days, which captures the speed of the semis rebound and has left many investors struggling to rebuild positions.
Amadeus: press reports Travelport stakeholders are discussing a combination with Sabre, which the desk calls positive for Amadeus.
Telenor: small negative from Telia's acquisition of the Telavox customer base, as Telavox traffic in Sweden and Norway likely moves to Telia.
SAP upgraded to Overweight by JPM (away from GS).
Auto Trader raised to Buy from Hold by Berenberg (away from GS).

sector_views.rationale: The SOX is up nearly 20% from its lows but about 25% below its YTD highs. The desk frames the debate as a bear-market bounce versus a mid-cycle correction, and sees buying so far in the US and not yet in Europe.

Telefonica and the German telecoms (UTDI, IONOS, 1&1, Freenet) reported mostly in-line to slightly beating quarters with guidance reiterated or raised. Telia's Telavox deal adds a small positive for Telia and a small negative for Telenor.
Stroer missed on Q3 revenue with weakness across all segments, and guidance is seen under pressure.

earnings_insights: Technoprobe Q3: revenue beat by 3% and EBITDA beat by 4% (reported vs consensus). Q4 revenue guidance of EUR270mn implies FY26 revenue of EUR1.05-1.065bn versus EUR1.1bn consensus.
Telefonica Q3: revenue beat by 1.3%, EBITDAaL beat by 1.7% (reported vs consensus). FCF reported EUR1.02bn versus consensus EUR821mn, including a EUR300mn tax benefit. Germany EBITDA was 2.2% light.

Telefonica FY guidance: revenue growth 1%-1.5% (from 1.5%-2.5%; 9M26 at 1.0%, Street 1.5%), adjusted EBITDA growth slightly above 2.5% (from 1.5%-2.5%; Street 2.6%), adjusted OpCFaL growth over 3.5% (from over 3%), FCF about EUR3.1bn (from about EUR3.0bn; Street EUR3bn), CapEx/revenue about 12%.

United Internet Q3: revenue 1% above consensus, EBITDA in line, guidance reiterated. IONOS in line with a slight EBITDA beat. 1&1 in line on revenue, EBITDA a beat excluding restructuring costs, capex a bit higher.
Freenet 3Q26: revenue and EBITDA broadly in line. FY26 FCF expected at the midpoint to upper end of the EUR270-300mn range versus EUR282mn company-compiled consensus. Guidance reiterated.

Stroer Q3: revenue EUR513mn, 2% below GS estimates and consensus. Organic growth 0.8% versus 3.8% expected by GS and Visible Alpha consensus. Operating EBITDA about EUR148mn, in line, with margin 28.8% versus 28.4% (GS) and 28.2% (consensus). Adjusted net income about EUR35mn versus GS estimate of EUR33mn.
Stroer FY26 guidance reiterated: low-to-mid-single-digit organic revenue growth (GS/consensus 3.4%/2.4%), adjusted EBITDA of about EUR626mn (GS/consensus EUR634mn/EUR632mn).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Index volatility continues to reset lower, supporting the Nasdaq 100 rebound.

risk_factors: Nvidia governance risk from the WSJ report on the board preparing to remove Jensen Huang.
The semis bounce may be a bear-market bounce rather than a durable recovery, with AI volatility persisting.
Political and local opposition to data-centre power costs after the midterms.
Telecom Italia/Swisscom and INWIT contract dispute remains unresolved.
AI agent restrictions: United Airlines is banning agents from flight reservations, with similar moves in banking.
vol_and_positioning: VIX at a 17 handle, with index volatility continuing to reset lower.
NDX up about 225bps on the day and back above its 200-day moving average and pre-election levels. The SOX is approaching its own 200-day moving average.
GS Prime: Systematic long/short funds posted their strongest two-day returns in almost three years.
The desk sees hedge funds and long-only investors starting to chase the US semis recovery, with no similar buying yet in Europe.
Callahan sees little consensus in market positioning and sentiment, a 'blank slate' going into 2027, with software dispersion up and Internet squeezy and hard to trade.
geopolitical: Post-midterm political risks and local opposition to data-centre power costs, addressed by Microsoft's pledge to pay its own way.
Italian authorities (AGCM, CONSOB, AGCOM) are involved in the INWIT and Telecom Italia/Swisscom tower contract dispute.
